discovery: Experimental discovery of the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect (zero-field fractional Chern insulators) in moiré transition-metal dichalcogenides
subfield: Condensed matter physics: topological quantum matter
motivation: For four decades, fractionally charged anyons were seen only in Landau levels at strong magnetic fields. Theorists proposed that topological flat Chern bands could host fractional quantum Hall states without any magnetic field. In 2023, the nominees found these fractional Chern insulators in twisted bilayer MoTe2. Xu and coworkers saw them first through optical and thermodynamic signatures and then through quantized fractional Hall transport at zero field. Mak and Shan, working independently, established them through compressibility and thermodynamic measurements. Their work showed that Chern bands produced by the moiré lattice and by spontaneous time-reversal breaking can stabilize fractionalized topological order. It opened a fast-growing field that includes fractional states in rhombohedral graphene, evidence for non-Abelian candidates, and new routes to anyons for topological quantum computing. This is the field's founding experiment, and it was guided closely by theory.
